summary: This version of the farmers' market app runs the same filtering, sorting, and mapping pipeline on a parallel stream, so the work can be split across multiple CPU cores. Because the pipeline only reads from the product list and collects into a fresh list, it stays thread-safe.

lines.text: The list starts empty; in the book the reader fills it with products where the comments below appear, so the printed output shows an empty result until that happens.
The main method simply hands the whole list to the helper, so all the stream logic lives in one place.
This is the only real change from the sequential version: parallelStream splits the data into chunks that the common ForkJoinPool processes at the same time.
Each product is tested independently and nothing outside the lambda is modified, which is exactly what makes a filter safe to run on many threads at once.
Sorting a parallel stream forces the results to be merged back into price order, so the parallel speedup is partly spent on that coordination — one reason parallel pays off only on large data sets.
The method reference pulls out each product's name, turning a stream of products into a stream of strings.
Collectors.toList handles the merging of per-thread partial results for you, so you never touch a shared list yourself and no synchronization is needed.
